channel.title: Marketplace Morning Report
channel.description: Get up to speed on the news each morning with our daily radio show and podcast, “Marketplace Morning Report,” hosted by Kimberly Adams. We give you the economy without the anxiety, in the amount of time it takes to brew a cup of coffee. Start your day with us, on air or by downloading our podcast, for context and perspective on the economic news that matters to you.

item.title: What the Deutsche Bank leak reveals
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
A new flood of leaked documents is putting fresh scrutiny on banking behemoth Deutsche Bank. The documents include more than 15 million internal emails and files, covering the early 2010s through 2021. A group of more than 200 journalists from around the globe has been analyzing the leaked information, revealing questionable practices, deals with Russian oligarchs, and more. Today, we hear from one of those reporters. But first, what did we get out of President Donald Trump's Asia summit?

item.title: Why JetBlue is in the red
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
Last week’s nationwide FAA ground stoppage hit JetBlue particularly hard. No other airline canceled a higher percentage of its flights than JetBlue, according to The Wall Street Journal. The company was already under pressure from investors worried about its heavy debt load and its struggles to turn a profit. What is the path forward for JetBlue? But first, when it comes to Federal Reserve rate hikes, size really does matter.

item.title: Affordability in Atlanta
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
This morning, we're continuing our "Economic Pulse" series conversation with Marlon Hyde, a business reporter at WABE in Atlanta. We're digging into the high cost of housing and recent community investments aimed at addressing the barriers to economic mobility. But first, the low-hire, low-fire job market shows no signs of letting up. That, plus concerns of a potential AI bubble, is certainly on the minds of Federal Reserve officials.

item.title: The toll of unpaid caregiving
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
KFF released a new survey on unpaid caregiving that finds that three in 10 adults have taken care of an aging, disabled, or chronically ill friend or family member in the last 12 months. About a quarter of those folks spend 15 hours a week doing it; nearly half work full-time. And it’s taking a toll — physical, emotional, and financial. Then, we learn why Atlanta has become a hub for data center construction.

item.title: The beneficiaries of Anthropic's IPO
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
Anthropic — the company behind the AI chatbot Claude — is going public tomorrow. When it starts trading on the Nasdaq, shares could be more than $80. This is projected to be one of the biggest initial public offerings ever, and long-time employees and early investors should expect a substantial payday. Also in this morning's podcast: a look at housing starts and the environmental threats from Alabama data center projects.

item.title: Kalshi, Trump, and fears of market manipulation
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
The prediction market platform Kalshi has stopped offering bets on whether President Donald Trump will say certain words in public speeches. This follows an order from federal regulators at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which says Kalshi needs to prove that these contracts are not “readily susceptible to manipulation." So far, Kalshi hasn’t done so. And later: a data center's risk to a rare fish species and the economics of "Grand Theft Auto VI."
